findings.reason: the plan's whole §3 migration route is chosen on a negative search result that the repo contradicts, and a corrected search changes materialise and derive from an ad-hoc REPL procedure to an extension of an existing mutation vocabulary.
findings.text: the plan's reuse map (comment c-20260917T151500-reuse-map-references) concludes "NO COMMITTED PYTHON SYMBOL WRITES THE REFERENCES EDGE" and from that plans per-pair inline Cypher through the REPL, but it missed RepairMutationKind, which already declares recompute_projection ("Recompute a scalar or relationship projection from live authority", standard_name.yaml:820) and add_relationship ("Materialize a relationship and its canonical properties", standard_name.yaml:816) — the plan's derive and materialise beats under another name — so the search was not exhausted before the plan declared the machinery absent

findings.reason: the derive-timing decision is argued from those per-reader effects, and if the cited lines no longer name those readers the decision's cost model is unverified and must be re-derived from the current symbols.
findings.text: the Decisions section asserts per-reader consequences from specific line citations that do not resolve to the described mechanism at HEAD: export.py:984 reads as a gate test-suite-failure append, not a reader that "would return only committed REFERENCES targets"; graph_ops.py:17122 (edit_status_before) does not undercount docs revisions; graph_ops.py:16477 (WITH sns2 AS sns) does not undercount refinement depth; graph_ops.py:12309 resolves only to a bare gc.query( call, not a PRODUCED_NAME reader; only doc_links.py:49 (find_name_references) and graph_ops.py:515 (inside _extract_links_from_docs' regex) match their stated roles — so five of seven prior-art citations are unchecked or stale, and the reader inventory behind the derive-timing decision rests on them

findings.reason: the plan should extend _apply_semantic_mirror_repair and the RepairMutationKind vocabulary rather than build a parallel per-pair route, or state why that owner cannot serve these pairs, otherwise two reconciliation paths drift under the fleet the §4 measure exists to keep consistent.
findings.text: _semantic_mirror_repair_authority (with _lock_semantic_mirror_repair_authority:21831, _semantic_mirror_repair_counts:21913, and _apply_semantic_mirror_repair at signed_manifest.py:6335) already owns exactly this plan's mechanism: it reconciles a semantic-source scalar mirror (a projected source_types/origin value) against its backing FROM_DD_PATH|FROM_SIGNAL to HAS_STANDARD_NAME projection closure, under a signed manifest, guards and receipts (SEMANTIC_MIRROR_REPAIR_MANIFEST_SCHEMA:21651) — the plan re-implements that reconciliation per pair in §3 instead of extending this owner, and the same owner covers §1's source_types, source_domains and origin mirrors

findings.reason: the plan cannot both add a second write path and claim §4's guarantee that a later census returns the same numbers, so the beats must land through the existing signed writer or explain the exception.
findings.text: the plan proposes materialising and removing REFERENCES edges and rewriting derived scalars without routing through the signed-manifest writer that owns every governed StandardName mutation (its edge allowlist already carries REFERENCES at signed_manifest.py:234, and apply_signed_manifest is the single mutation entry point graph_ops.py uses), so the materialise-adjudicate-derive beats fork the commit and receipt path the graph already treats as authoritative

findings.reason: a single module over the existing repair primitives removes the per-node beat-restatement and is the shape the twelve-pair surface actually wants; leaving it spread is the shallow-wrapper explosion this rubric item exists to catch.
findings.text: the plan scatters one operation — recompute a mirrored scalar from its authoritative relationship — across twelve pairs, each its own node with its own beat accounting (§3 "One pair per node"), and mentions "one shared authority predicate" only for the review-timestamp pair (scalar-retention rationale) without generalising it, so the same three beats and the same parity digests are re-specified per pair instead of hidden behind one interface that takes (scalar, relationship, derivation) and performs materialise, adjudicate and derive once

findings.reason: if the producer owns reference discovery it should own the edge write it implies, which turns the materialise beat from a separate migration into a producer extension and removes the 83-fossil class the parity refresh had to adjudicate by hand.
findings.text: the materialise beat uses _extract_links_from_docs (the committed scalar producer) only to regenerate the scalar for a parity comparison, and the plan does not say why that producer cannot be extended to emit the REFERENCES edge it derives from the same parsed documentation, so the plan adds a one-off comparison wrapper over machinery that already parses the source rather than extending the parse site

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the plan spreads one mechanism (materialise, adjudicate, derive a mirrored scalar) across twelve pairs and many nodes rather than behind one module, and names a "shared authority predicate" for one pair without generalising it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements scalar-mirror reconciliation that imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py and signed_manifest.py already own as a signed, guarded, receipted repair.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; every section retires scalar properties and re-points readers at relationships, adds no member of any of the four families, and needs no retirement statement.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched for a writer of the REFERENCES edge but never found the governed repair framework, whose RepairMutationKind already declares recompute_projection and add_relationship, and several prior-art claims in its Decisions do not resolve to the cited code at HEAD.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the materialise beat re-runs the existing scalar producer to compute a comparison value rather than saying why that producer cannot own the edge write.
